preamble: Twelve solutions are cloth hats and may be partially clued.

clue.text: A Lammas Day return

indicators.note: return means the two pieces before it are read backwards as one run

parts.note: the article a can also be written an
Lammas Day falls on 1 August, written as AUG I

explanation.surface: Someone marks the harvest festival by coming home on Lammas Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reads the whole run backwards. Lammas Day is an old English harvest festival held on the first of August.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble's theme of twelve reptiles supplies this tropical American lizard; the clue gives only wordplay.

clue.text: Devil does effect lacking spontaneity

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: to effect is to bring about, here a rearrangement of the word does

explanation.surface: A demon carries out some impressive act, though it all feels forced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'effect' is the anagram signal: to effect is to bring about, here a fresh order for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imposed is forced on people from outside rather than arising naturally, so it lacks spontaneity.

clue.text: Going too far from useful trade

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the words useful trade

explanation.surface: Someone warns against overreaching in a profitable line of business.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra as an adjective or prefix means extreme, beyond the usual bounds.

clue.text: Gunners worried about initiation of little baby

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other
worried suggests the word gunners being agitated into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: the initiation of a word is its opening, here its first two letters

explanation.surface: Artillerymen fret about introducing a tiny infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container; 'initiation of' takes the opening pair of letters, as Araucaria often does, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurseling is an infant still being nursed, so a synonym for a baby.

clue.text: A little bit of poetry amid the silence?

indicators.note: amid means set in the middle of the silence word

parts.note: mum is an old word for silence, as in mum's the word
odic is the adjective meaning relating to an ode

explanation.surface: A scrap of verse is murmured during a quiet moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amid' is the container signal. Mum meaning silence survives in the phrase 'keep mum'; 'bit' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small quantity of something, just a little bit.

clue.text: Senior pupil on TV

definitions.meaning: a pupil given duties of oversight in a school
a television screen or display used for watching output

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the monitor lizard, one of the twelve reptiles.
explanation.definitionFit: A school prefect can be called this, and so can a screen or display set.

clue.text: Miller's answer?

parts.note: anyone surnamed Miller is traditionally nicknamed after the flour on a miller's clothes

explanation.walkthrough: British nickname convention pairs a surname with a fixed nickname: Millers get this one, from flour-covered millers.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional nickname for a Miller, because millers were covered in flour dust.

clue.text: Church sign in its response

indicators.note: in means the sign is placed inside the response

parts.note: the congregation's response to a prayer in church is amen
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A star sign turns up in the congregation's reply during a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'its response' means the church's response, the congregational reply to a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lizard famed for changing colour, one of the twelve reptiles the preamble supplies with no defining word.

clue.text: He robs one in the street, which is a facer

definitions.text: He robs one in the street
definitions.meaning: a street robber who attacks passers-by
one who mugs, that is pulls faces

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the mugger crocodile of India, one of the twelve reptiles.
explanation.definitionFit: A street robber is called this, and so is someone who mugs or pulls faces.

clue.text: Grand place for a bank account!

definitions.text: Grand place for a bank account!

parts.words: Grand place for a bank account!
parts.note: Grand ... is a Caribbean island famous for offshore banking

explanation.walkthrough: Grand Cayman is the largest of the Cayman Islands, a tax haven; the reptile is a crocodilian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cayman Islands are a well-known offshore banking centre; the reptile is a South American crocodilian.

clue.text: Cabinet minister, French marshal keeping her out

indicators.note: keeping means the marshal's name holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Philippe Pétain was a Marshal of France

indicators.note: out means the letters of her are put out of order

explanation.surface: A government minister is likened to a French soldier who excludes a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal and 'keeping' the container. Peter Hain was a British Labour cabinet minister; Pétain the First World War marshal.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Hain served in Labour cabinets, so he is an example of a cabinet minister.

clue.text: Common words set to music about local leader

indicators.note: about means one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: sang can mean set words to music

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of local

explanation.surface: Everyday lyrics are performed around a regional figurehead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L, the first letter of 'local' picked out by 'leader', inside SANG.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal, everyday vocabulary, so common words in the sense of colloquial ones.

clue.text: Is without cover and identification?

annotationWithheld.why: Is without cover and identification?: IS NAKED less I and D gives the answer, but 'without' must give NAKED (without cover) and also signal removing ID, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Alcoholic compound of setter and solver's spare report

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me
the solver is addressed as you, so solver's is thy

indicators.note: report means what follows is how a word sounds when spoken

parts.note: spare as in thin means lean

explanation.surface: A chemist describes a compound linking the setter, the solver and a lean account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' asks for the sound of LEAN, spelt LENE; methylene is the radical in methyl alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Methylene is a chemical group found in compounds related to methyl alcohol.

clue.text: Sign missing from reference books, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: missing from means the sign is taken out of the books word

parts.note: dictionaries are reference books
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A star sign has gone from the encyclopedias, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing from' removes ARIES from DICTIONARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is the way someone pronounces and chooses words, so their manner of speaking.

clue.text: School kids walking promise subsequent meeting with …

definitions.meaning: a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs
the playground reply 'in a while' to 'see you later, alligator'

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs into 16 down: 'See you later, alligator' gets the reply 'In a while, crocodile', a promise to meet later.
explanation.definitionFit: A file of pupils walking two by two is called this, and it is the reptile in the rhyme.

clue.text: You are red from embarrassment

indicators.note: embarrassment suggests letters thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: Someone tells you that you are blushing with shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embarrassment' signals the anagram of ARE RED; 'You' is the person reading the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The person reading any printed text, including this clue, is its reader.

clue.text: … everyone a prince at heart

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: heart means the word at goes into the centre of the prince's name

parts.note: Prince Igor is the hero of Borodin's opera

explanation.surface: All of us are royalty deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' is the container signal and 'a' is only a link. Prince Igor is the title hero of Borodin's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A large American crocodilian, one of the preamble's twelve reptiles; the clue continues the rhyme begun at 14 down.

clue.text: Mythical member (at least in part) of the twelve, fool with right good heart

indicators.note: heart means placed in the middle of the fool word

parts.note: a goon is a fool

explanation.surface: A legendary member of a group of twelve is a fool with a kind heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' puts R and G in the middle of GOON; the Gorgon, with snakes for hair, is partly one of the twelve reptiles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gorgons are monsters of Greek myth, such as Medusa, so mythical figures.

clue.text: Northern lingua franca making hammer superfluous?

indicators.note: franca means free, so the letters of lingua are set loose

explanation.surface: A shared northern language somehow does away with the need for a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'franca' is the anagram signal: in lingua franca it means free or Frankish, so the word is set loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A power tool that drives nails, doing a hammer's work for it.

clue.text: Vegetable finishes telescoped on the first

parts.note: kale is a green vegetable

indicators.note: telescoped means the two words overlap, sharing a letter

parts.note: ends are finishes

explanation.surface: A vegetable finally ends up on the menu on the first of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'telescoped' joins KALE and ENDS on their shared E.
explanation.definitionFit: The kalends were the first day of the month in the Roman calendar.

clue.text: Kick-off time and the party has tediously to continue

parts.note: mo is a moment, a short time
a do is a party
to drag on is to continue tediously

explanation.surface: After the kick-off the party drags on endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: The four pieces make the largest lizard; the reptile itself is given by the preamble.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest living lizard, from Indonesia, supplied as one of the twelve reptiles named in the preamble.

clue.text: Girl died with cry of triumph during immoral act

indicators.note: during means put inside the immoral act

parts.note: a sin is an immoral act
OB is short for obiit, Latin for died
ha is a cry of triumph

explanation.surface: A young woman perished shouting in triumph in the middle of wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is the container signal. OB, from Latin obiit, is the usual abbreviation for died on gravestones and in records.
explanation.definitionFit: Siobhan is an Irish girl's name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: It takes light years to analyse a number

parts.note: to parse a sentence is to analyse it
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Breaking down a figure takes forever.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is about 3.26 light years, a distance light takes over three years to cross.

clue.text: Translated, I love the poor shrimp's deficiency of structure

parts.note: amo is Latin for I love

indicators.note: poor suggests the shrimp is knocked into another shape

parts.note: the letters of shrimp as written, the possessive adding none

explanation.surface: Someone declares love for a pitiful crustacean that lacks a proper shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translated' asks for Latin; 'poor' rearranges SHRIMP into RPHISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorphism is the state of having no definite form, a lack of structure.

clue.text: Fireside game?

definitions.meaning: a tool kept by the hearth for stirring coals
a card game played for stakes

explanation.definitionFit: A fire iron for stirring coals and a gambling card game share this name.

clue.text: Purveyors of electricity to stun?

parts.note: GEC was the General Electric Company, a British firm
KO, a knockout, stuns

explanation.surface: Electricity suppliers deliver a stunning jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: GEC was a big British electrical company; KO is a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: A small climbing lizard able to walk on walls, one of the twelve reptiles left undefined by the clue.

clue.text: Held on to carbonised source of air

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
the lung supplies air to the body

explanation.surface: Someone clung to a blackened breathing organ.
explanation.definitionFit: To have clung is to have held on to something tightly.

clue.text: Self-starter's peculiarity

parts.note: the starter of self is its first letter S
a kink is a quirk or peculiarity

explanation.surface: An entrepreneur has an odd quirk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Self-starter' looks like a go-getter but means the start of 'Self'.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-scaled burrowing lizard, one of the twelve reptiles the preamble supplies instead of a definition.

clue.text: Move to show pride in Lawrence's full interjection

parts.note: to go is to move

indicators.note: in means placed inside the writer's initials

parts.note: D. H. Lawrence was an English novelist
to strut is to walk with pride

explanation.surface: A gesture of pride in a novelist's exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'full' matters: strewth is the clipped form of this oath, so the definition asks for the unabridged one.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath of surprise, the full form behind the clipped exclamation strewth.

clue.text: Award for service in Guevara/Reagan contest?

parts.note: Che Guevara the revolutionary
v for versus marks a contest
Ronald Reagan, Ron for short

explanation.surface: A medal for a matchup between the revolutionary and the president.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the slash as a pairing: v for versus sits between the two first names. A chevron is worn on the sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is a V-shaped stripe on a sleeve marking rank or length of service.

clue.text: See 19 down
